findings.title: CMEK-encrypted Dataflow job has no companion IAM grant for the Dataflow service agent or the worker service account on its KMS key
findings.explanation: Re-verified 2026-08-09: iam.tf now contains both google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.dataflow_service_agent (grants the Dataflow Service Agent decrypt access) and google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.dataflow_worker_kms (grants the same to the dedicated worker service account), both keyed off var.kms_key_name, and google_dataflow_job.main explicitly depends_on both. The gap this finding originally caught is closed.

findings.title: google_storage_bucket_iam_member.template grants access on a GCS object path, not a bucket — the objectViewer grant silently never resolves to a valid IAM binding
findings.explanation: iam.tf:35 sets `bucket = var.template_gcs_path`, but that variable holds a full gs:// object path (variables.tf documents it as "GCS path to the Dataflow job template", and google_dataflow_job.main.tf:3 correctly consumes it as the job's template_gcs_path attribute). The `bucket` argument on google_storage_bucket_iam_member requires a bare bucket name — exactly what the sibling grant temp_gcs uses one line below (`bucket = var.bucket_name`, iam.tf:41). In the shipped example, module.dataflow.tf:9 sets template_gcs_path = "gs://${google_storage_bucket.dataflow.name}/templates/example", so this resource's bucket attribute becomes a GCS URI with a path segment — the Storage API rejects that as an invalid bucket name at apply time (bucket names cannot contain "/" or a scheme prefix). A rules engine can't catch this: HLD_GCP_018/039/210 (the only policies covering google_storage_bucket_iam_member) check the member/role, not whether the bucket argument is even a syntactically valid bucket name, and confirming the mismatch requires tracing template_gcs_path's value across the module boundary into the example's own bucket wiring — this is a same-shape regression to the one HLD_GCP_483 was written to catch, just on the storage side instead of the KMS side. Blast radius: apply fails outright on this resource, so the Dataflow worker SA never receives objectViewer on the template bucket regardless of whether template_gcs_path happens to share a bucket with bucket_name.
findings.remediation: Change iam.tf:35 to `bucket = var.bucket_name`, matching the sibling temp_gcs grant — the module already assumes a single bucket_name serves both temp and template storage (see HOLDEN_AI_003, which flags what that shared-bucket assumption implies for the temp_gcs grant's scope).

findings.title: objectAdmin grant for temp storage is scoped to the whole bucket, not a prefix — once HOLDEN_AI_002 is fixed, the narrower template objectViewer grant becomes a no-op whenever bucket_name and the template's bucket coincide
findings.explanation: google_storage_bucket_iam_member.temp_gcs grants roles/storage.objectAdmin (read/write/delete) on the entire var.bucket_name bucket, with no IAM condition scoping it to temp_gcs_location's own path prefix (GCS IAM supports resource.name.startsWith(...) conditions for exactly this). The module's own example wires bucket_name, template_gcs_path, and temp_gcs_location to the same underlying bucket (google_storage_bucket.dataflow) at three different path prefixes (root, templates/, tmp/). Once HOLDEN_AI_002 is fixed and the template grant correctly targets that same bucket, the worker SA's effective permission on the template objects is objectAdmin (from temp_gcs, unscoped) — the objectViewer grant intended to keep the worker read-only on templates provides no actual restriction, because a broader admin grant on the same resource already subsumes it. This is a composition a rules engine can't see: each grant is individually a reasonable role for its stated purpose, and nothing in either resource's own attributes reveals that they land on the same bucket in typical usage — only the combination, and the templates' actual location, exposes that the intended least-privilege split has no effect.
findings.remediation: Add an IAM condition to temp_gcs scoping objectAdmin to the temp_gcs_location prefix (e.g. condition { expression = "resource.name.startsWith(\"projects/_/buckets/${var.bucket_name}/objects/tmp/\")" ... }), or document that callers should use a separate bucket for templates vs. temp storage if a real read-only boundary on templates is required. Which approach is right depends on whether template/temp separation is meant to be enforced by this module or left to the caller's bucket layout — a judgment call, not a mechanical fix.

suggested_policies.rationale: google_storage_bucket_iam_member.bucket (and the analogous google_storage_bucket_iam_binding.bucket) must be a bare GCS bucket name — the Storage API rejects a gs:// URI or any value containing a "/" with an apply-time error, since bucket names cannot contain a scheme prefix or path separator. HOLDEN_AI_002 in this repo is exactly this shape: a GCS object-path variable passed where a bucket-name variable belongs. This is a general, resource-type-and-attribute-scoped, unambiguous check (regex format), not specific to this repo's variables, and none of the three existing policies covering google_storage_bucket_iam_member (HLD_GCP_018, HLD_GCP_039, HLD_GCP_210) check the bucket attribute's own format — they check member/role only.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_002
name: Storage bucket IAM member/binding bucket must be a bare bucket name, not a GCS path
principle: identity-and-access
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  google_storage_bucket_iam_member and google_storage_bucket_iam_binding's
  bucket argument must be a bare GCS bucket name. A gs:// URI or any value
  containing a path segment (e.g. a template or object path mistakenly
  passed instead of the bucket name) is rejected by the Storage API at
  apply time with an invalid-bucket-name error, so the intended IAM grant
  never takes effect — Terraform accepts the configuration, but the API
  does not.
remediation: |
  Pass the bucket's bare name (e.g. google_storage_bucket.example.name, or
  a variable documented and validated as a bucket name) rather than a
  gs://bucket/path value.
resources:
  google_storage_bucket_iam_member:
    path: bucket
    not_matches: "^gs://|/"
  google_storage_bucket_iam_binding:
    path: bucket
    not_matches: "^gs://|/"
